objective: Replace CalVCB's custom-coded CaRes claims system with a highly configurable claims, compensation, and restitution platform, so victims are served through agile, end-to-end workflows that adapt to policy and statutory change (§1.C, §1.D).
challenges: 1. Lack of agility in making updates or additions to functionality; changes depend heavily on coding
2. No adjustments module; returned payments require code updates and depend on external databases
3. No appeals workflow; appeals are tracked through external, manually integrated processes
4. No correspondence engine; letters are hard coded, manual, and only available in English and Spanish
5. No attribute-level audit trail of who took what action at each phase
6. Online application process is external and not integrated with the system of record
7. Uploaded data and documents cannot be renamed; must be re-uploaded to correct a name
8. No integration between claim and provider information
9. Separation of duties is managed manually with no system warnings or notifications
10. Lack of agility in producing customized reports in a timely manner

deliverables: One configurable claims, compensation, and restitution system; COTS, MOTS, integrated products, or custom all considered equally
End-to-end coverage: intake, eligibility, emergency awards, bill review with auto-payment rules, appeals, adjustments, restitution and offender tracking, correspondence
350-400 role-based users across CalVCB headquarters and county JP and CRC offices
Configurable workflows, rules, letters, and reports changed without custom coding
Integrated online application intake, replacing the current external process
Active claims migrated with full history and supporting documents
Attribute-level audit trail and automated separation-of-duties controls

rfiSummary.procurementObjective: Decide the solution approach (COTS, MOTS, integrated product set, COTS Configurable, or custom), with no stated preference; phased vs. single cutover and technology replacement vs. broader business transformation also remain open (§1.A; Att. 3 Q8, Q25, Q27, Q50, Q51).

challengeThemes.detail: Functionality, correspondence, and reporting changes all depend on coding and take months, with no major enhancements in three years (items 1, 4, 10).
No adjustments, appeals, or correspondence modules, and the online application and provider data sit outside the system of record (items 2, 3, 4, 6, 8).
No action-level audit trail and separation of duties is enforced manually with no system warnings (items 5, 9).
Documents cannot be renamed after upload and correspondence is limited to English and Spanish (items 4, 7).

consequences: Higher number of phone calls and emails
Lack of visibility into status or progress
Inconsistent information across divisions, claimants, providers and advocates
Increased time to approval and payment
rfiSummary.endState: A single configurable system covering the full claims, compensation, and restitution lifecycle: intake (online, mail, email), eligibility determination, emergency awards, bill review with an auto-payment rules engine, appeals, returned-benefit adjustments against lifetime limits, restitution and offender tracking, and multilingual correspondence. It serves 350-400 role-based users at CalVCB headquarters and county JP and CRC offices, with JP staff processing applications and bills directly in the system and CRC staff managing criminal dispositions. It integrates at minimum with the existing Bill Review Service, the State Controller's Office, the Franchise Tax Board, EDD, and TotalAgility, and migrates active claims with full history and supporting documents from CaRes; external databases are excluded from migration.
endStateConstraints: Must at minimum support the existing bill-adjudication interface; integrated adjudication may be considered (Att. 3 Q11)
State data center, CDT-approved cloud, or vendor California-compliant cloud all acceptable (Att. 3 Q6, Q26)
NIST 800-53, FISMA, and SAM 5300 apply; no CJIS or IRS 1075 requirement (Att. 2; Att. 3 Q29, Q30)
Any GenAI use must follow SIMM 5305-F and SAM 5300 (Att. 3 Q33)
External databases are out of migration scope; active claims plus full history and documents are in scope (Att. 3 Q17)
No budget, funding range, or implementation timeline established (Att. 3 Q2, Q10, Q12, Q20, Q21, Q31, Q35)
Non-binding cost model requested, broken down by one-time vs. recurring, module, and phase (§1.F; Att. 1 Part V; Att. 3 Q9)
rfiSummary.nextStep: Invite-only demonstrations in October 2026, with success criteria not yet established; a future solicitation is anticipated on Cal eProcure (§1.G, §1.H; Att. 3 Q34).

issuerQuestions.question: Does the 10-page limit in Attachment 1 include the worksheet's own question text, Part I company information, and the signature block, or only the respondent's answers?
issuerQuestions.basis: The limit applies to the total submission, but the worksheet itself spans several pages of questions and forms.

issuerQuestions.question: Section 1.F references written responses including the Attachment 1 worksheet, while Att. 3 Q49 prohibits supplemental appendices or attachments; may respondents include a brief cover letter, and does it count toward the 10-page limit?
issuerQuestions.basis: The RFI implies content may accompany the worksheet, but the Q&A forbids supplemental materials outright.

issuerQuestions.question: For Q48, should data cleansing and remediation be included in the base cost estimate or presented as an optional/separate line item?
issuerQuestions.basis: The answer 'These have not been established. Yes.' does not clarify which treatment applies.

issuerQuestions.question: Are exchanges with the Department of Justice, crime-reporting agencies, and courts in scope as required system integrations?
issuerQuestions.basis: The RFI narrative describes these exchanges as part of eligibility determination, but the Q&A integration list omits them.

issuerQuestions.question: Is the external online application service intended to be replaced by the new solution, or integrated with it going forward?
issuerQuestions.basis: Challenge item 6 flags the external online process as a gap, but it is absent from the Q&A's list of integrations.

issuerQuestions.question: Beyond the 350-400 internal, JP, and CRC users, how many external users (claimants, providers, advocates, court personnel) should respondents assume for capacity and licensing?
issuerQuestions.basis: The RFI cites about 300 users, the Q&A confirms 350-400 internal/county users, but external-user figures in Q47 were not answered.
